title: Reconcile transient cross-tenant billing spikes from overlapping credential handoffs and subproject aliasing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Observed short-lived (3-12 minute) billing spikes that are attributed to the wrong workspace after a sequence where a customer promotes a subproject and an API key rotation occurs within the same 60s window. The incorrect attribution reliably shows as a burst of embedded/LLM tokens attributed to the promoting workspace rather than the original tenant.

Observed impact:
- Erroneous per-tenant token counts reported in billing aggregator for 1-2 billing windows (~5–15 minutes).
- Affected customers see spikes in usage and alerts from internal cost monitors.
- Downstream billing reconciliation job corrects amounts later, but customers receive alarming emails/alerts and support load increases.

Hypothesis / Root cause candidates:
1) Claim cache staleness: when an API key is rotated and a subproject is promoted at near-simultaneous times, the claim-to-workspace mapping cache returns the old binding for some proxy workers while other workers observe the new binding, producing mixed attribution.
2) Attribution key granularity: rate-limiter and metering dedupe keys do not include credential-epoch or promotion-epoch, so counters from two short-lived identities collapse onto the same bucket used by the promoted subproject.
3) NAT/proxy reuse: ephemeral proxy connections reuse the same TCP 5-tuple; telemetry aggregated by connection reloader can join requests across credential boundaries.

Repro steps (local / staging):
1) Create tenant A with project a1 and tenant B with project b1.
2) Start steady low-rate LLM traffic under a1.
3) Rotate API key for a1 while simultaneously triggering a promotion that moves a1 -> a1-promoted alias (simulate within 30s).
4) Inject a short burst (200–500 concurrent requests over 60s) from a client machine using the old key immediately before rotation and the new key after rotation.
5) Observe attribution in billing-aggregator and rate-limiter logs (use debug flags). Expected: a measurable fraction of the burst attributed incorrectly to a1-promoted.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Paused automated alert emails for affected customers while we investigate to reduce noise.
- Launched ad-hoc reconciliation job to diff token counts between raw ingress logs (per-request auth claims) and aggregated counters; corrected ledger entries for two customers already.
- Enabled higher-fidelity tracing on a narrow set of front proxies to capture claim header/epoch for 24 hours.

Planned fix / implementation steps:
1) Reproduce reliably in a dedicated staging scenario and add an automated integration test that simulates overlapping rotation+promotion with bursts. (Owner: Diego)
2) Change metering/rate-limiter dedupe key to include credential_epoch and promotion_epoch (or a monotonic claim_version). This prevents counter collapse across handoffs. (Owner: Runtime team)
3) Harden cache invalidation: ensure claim cache invalidation is propagated synchronously to edge workers for keys with active sessions; add short-lived TTLs for keys undergoing rotation/promotion. (Owner: Auth/Core)
4) Add metrics and a Grafana panel for "attribution-consistency" that compares per-request claim-derived workspace_id vs aggregated workspace attribution for the same time window; alert on >0.5% mismatch. (Owner: Observability)
5) Backfill reconciliation job to run hourly for 48 hours after deploy and weekly thereafter for 2 weeks. (Owner: Billing)
6) Ship runtime patch behind a gradual rollout flag and monitor. (Owner: Runtime/Infra)

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration test passes that simulates rotations + promotions under burst and shows no cross-tenant attribution >0.1% after fix.
- Production canary shows elimination of transient mismatches; reconciliation job reports zero post-correction deltas for canary tenants.
- Grafana alert triggers on an injected fault and is exercised in runbook.
